title: Filesystem socket helpers are socket-only and authority-conscious
summary: Pathname helpers deliberately refuse generic filesystem mutation. chmod/chown pin a verified socket inode with O_PATH|O_NOFOLLOW before mutation; unlink verifies a socket and refuses ordinary files but still depends on parent-directory authority.
invariants: Never silently unlink an arbitrary pre-existing path during bind.
chmodSocketPath and chownSocketPath must not become generic chmod/chown helpers.
O_PATH|O_NOFOLLOW plus stat verification pins the inode used for chmod/chown on the qualified Linux profile.
unlinkPath refuses non-sockets, but Linux has no general unlink-by-open-fd primitive; safe deployment must control the parent directory.
Socket-option mutation is an explicit whitelist, not an arbitrary setsockopt escape hatch.
procedure: Treat creation/removal of pathname sockets as filesystem authority operations, not merely socket API calls.

provenance.claim: Path helpers inspect socket inode type, pin chmod/chown targets with O_PATH|O_NOFOLLOW, refuse non-socket safe-unlink, and keep raw unlink separate.
